thread:
mia: Heads up — multiple OOMs on prod-dedicated-us-east-3 (gpu-pool-b). Started ~12:02 UTC after a burst of long-context requests.
ankit: Confirming. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/prod-inference?view=mem spike to 98% then cuda OOMs.
franz: infra-bot fired: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` on node gpu-pool-b-12. We need a fast soft-landing.
maya: Triage plan (fast):
  1) Immediately divert non-critical traffic to fallback small-quant model (reduce memory footprint).
  2) Temporarily disable batching on affected hosts (set batch_size=1) to avoid accumulation.
  3) Enable aggressive KV eviction (ttl=30s) and drop prefix cache for long sequences.
  4) Flip circuit breaker for seq_len>1024 to force light path.
franz: Commands:
```
# divert traffic for standard tier
rctl route update prod-inference --match 'tier:standard' --dest model=fallback-small
# live toggle batching on node group
api patch /runtime/nodes/gpu-pool-b --body '{"batching": {"max_batch_size": 1}}'
# KV eviction (experimental):
redis-cli -h kv-cache-prod HSET node:gpu-pool-b eviction_ttl 30
```
ankit: Doing (1) & (2) now. Patching batching + route. Posting logs in a sec.
infra-bot: patch applied: batching.max_batch_size=1 on gpu-pool-b (req_id=tx-88ff). Route update started (req_id=tx-88gg).
mia: After diversion latency for fallback-small looks fine; memory usage dropped ~12% on pool B. But we still have intermittent OOM on a couple of pods.
franz: For the remaining pods: quick kernel swap to quantized U8 kernel and disable workspace preallocation for small-heap hosts. That usually recovers residual OOMs.
maya: Kernel swap command (do carefully):
```
# mark node for kernel swap to quant-u8
ctl nodes annotate gpu-pool-b-12 kernel_preference=quant-u8 --dry-run=false
# disable prealloc
api patch /runtime/hosts/gpu-pool-b-12 --body '{"workspace": {"preallocate": false}}'
```
oncall-joe: I'm oncall — I'm going to cordon the two worst nodes and force pods to reschedule after we apply kernel swap so they come up smaller.
ankit: Also enabling temporary request-shaping: reject requests with prompt_tokens > 2500 with 413 until we stabilize.
mia: Agree, set soft rejection with guidance message to clients.
franz: Added a short-term rollout checklist to incident channel: monitor OOM rate, avg mem per request, and tail latency. If OOM rate doesn't drop to < 0.5/hr in 15m, escalate to full-scale drain and repro on staging.
maya: Note — document regression hypothesis: recent kernel-selector change (auto-favor fast-fp16 kernel) sometimes picks a kernel that preallocs larger workspace for long sequences. That aligns with timing of last canary.
ankit: Capturing heap traces and kernel selection logs: `/var/log/runtime/kernel-select.log` pushed to S3 at s3://redwood-incidents/3051234567/kernel-logs.tar.gz
infra-bot: Alert: one pod restarted due to OOM (pod gpu-worker-87) — back up on fallback-small.
mia: Status update: after the swap + eviction + batching=1, OOM events dropped to 0 in the last 10m. Rolling the kernel-swap to remaining nodes slowly.
franz: Postmortem action items:
  - Revert heuristic that prefers that specific fp16 kernel for seq_len>512 unless memory check passes.
  - Add a pre-deploy memory-probing test that runs short warmups to estimate workspace for new kernels.
  - Add an emergency soft-landing policy that automatically diverts 30-50% traffic to fallback-small when node mem>90%.
  - Improve observability: track per-model workspace footprints over time and alert on percent delta >20%.
maya: I'll file the PRs tonight for the probe test and the policy.
oncall-joe: Thanks everyone, moving to monitoring-only. Closing thread in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:
franz: Great work — quick, surgical mitigations. We'll follow up with a concise incident write-up.
